title: Increasing Target Plasma Bicarbonate (HCO₃) Concentrations for Lung-Protective Ventilation in Individuals with Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) requiring Continuous Kidney Replacement Therapy (CKRT) (The BigBic Study II)
summary: The study aims to improve lung-protective ventilation in ARDS patients undergoing continuous renal replacement therapy (CVVHD) by increasing the bicarbonate target. ARDS leads to severe respiratory failure and pulmonary edema, and lung-protective ventilation with low tidal volumes reduces mortality but often causes hypercapnia and acidosis. Normally, the kidneys compensate by reabsorbing bicarbonate, which is limited in cases of acute kidney failure. The study seeks to raise the bicarbonate target in CVVHD from 24 mmol/l to 30 mmol/l to allow better tolerance of hypercapnia and enable lung-protective ventilation.
conditions: Other and unspecified abnormalities of breathing

interventions.name: Modified citrate-based continuous kidney replacement therapy aiming for a plasma HCO₃ concentration of 30mmol/l by adaption of the blood to dialysate ratio.
Standard citrate-based continuous renal replacement therapy with a conventional target plasma HCO₃ concentration of 24mmol/l.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-	Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS)
-	Invasive ventilation
-	Citrate-based continuous kidney replacement therapy
Exclusion criteria:
-	Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation
-	Severe liver failure (bilirubin > 8mg/dl and INR>2)
-	Severe lactic acidosis (lactate > 80mg/dl)
